tasks.short: Agree who owns project work, confirm capacity and record responsibilities.

steps.what: Review unassigned tasks, required skills and existing responsibilities.
Reconcile staff availability and existing allocations in the capacity sheet.
Discuss suitable ownership, workload and support needs with staff.
Resolve competing demands and approve staff allocation with the line manager.
Explain responsibilities, decision limits and handovers to the assigned staff.
Record agreed ownership and responsibilities in the project records.

tasks.design: A deterministic integration combines declared availability from {HCM} with assignments in {PROJECT} to replace the capacity workbook. People discuss ownership and approve allocation, then configured forms in {PROJECT} capture responsibilities and publish agreed records. No model is needed for this design.
tasks.previous_blocker: Capacity data crossed organisational boundaries and often needed manual correction. Selecting an owner depended on context that a capacity sheet could not capture.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations and existing assignment forms can remove reconciliation and recording effort. These improvements do not depend on automated staff selection.
tasks.still_hard: Fair workload, development opportunities, specialist fit and competing line-management priorities remain human judgements. GDPR and national employment and consultation rules shape access to staffing data.
tasks.human_edge: The project manager recognises when someone needs support, negotiates competing demands and establishes clear responsibility without damaging trust.
tasks.altitude: The week gains some time from capacity checks and recording, while allocation discussions remain substantial. Nothing changes in decision rights; line managers still approve staff commitments.

reach.task: Resolve shared-service capacity conflicts across projects.
reach.learn: Service priorities, allocation limits and how project commitments affect routine operations.

reach.task: Agree technical ownership and handover responsibilities.
reach.learn: Technical skill requirements, review duties and the boundaries between delivery and operational ownership.

evidence.claim: Declared capacity and current allocations can be reconciled deterministically; choosing staff still requires contextual judgement.
Keeping employee selection human and omitting model-based ranking avoids introducing AI selection into this design.
The proposed effort reductions are estimates; the supplied digest contains no direct staff-allocation implementation case.

assumptions: A capacity workbook connects {HCM} availability to assignments in {PROJECT}.
Only declared availability and agreed allocations are needed; medical details are excluded.
Line managers approve staff commitments in this typical matrix organisation.
The low-drudgery prior is retained: most time stays in discussion, allocation and explanation.
The integration identifies capacity conflicts but does not score employee performance or select workers.
Build ranges cover one staffing pool and exclude external waiting.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. National rules determine consultation and employment requirements.
unknowns: Whether the organisation uses matrix allocation or delegates assignment rights to project managers.
How reliable availability and allocation records are across projects.
Which staffing fields project managers may access.
Whether the proposed integration requires employee or works-council consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which capacity checks catch double-booking without exposing unnecessary employee data?
Can native assignment forms capture decision limits and handovers clearly?
Does the capacity view support fair allocation without encouraging excessive utilisation?
new_work: Review conflicting or stale capacity records.
Maintain allocation calendars and access permissions.
Record approved exceptions to capacity limits.
Check that responsibility records match the agreements made with staff.
tasks.statement: Assign duties or responsibilities to project personnel.

tasks.short: Agree project requirements and objectives with stakeholders.

steps.what: Read the project brief, previous decisions and stakeholder requests.

loop.input: Project brief, decision log and stakeholder requests.
loop.output: Source-linked objectives, constraints, conflicts and open questions.
loop.check: Require a source reference for each claim; flag conflicting statements for review.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document batch; unresolved items enter the discussion brief.
loop.why_not_simpler: Objectives and constraints arrive in varied prose; fixed fields cannot capture existing documents reliably.

steps.what: Arrange stakeholder sessions and circulate the discussion brief.
Discuss needs, uncover disagreements and negotiate project priorities.
Write requirements, acceptance criteria and unresolved questions.

loop.input: Workshop notes, proposed priorities and project brief.
loop.output: Requirements draft with acceptance criteria and explicit unresolved questions.
loop.check: Link requirements to notes; separate agreed statements from proposals; review acceptance criteria.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing agreement stays unresolved rather than being inferred.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning informal discussion into testable requirements needs interpretation and writing.

steps.what: Approve the scope and objectives, or return disputed requirements.

tasks.design: A configured flow in the {CALENDAR} arranges sessions, while a bounded loop turns approved material in the {DOCS} into a discussion brief and requirements draft. The {PROJECT} links each requirement to its source and records sponsor approval before establishing the baseline.
tasks.previous_blocker: The difficult part was reaching agreement. Preparation and documentation also required reading inconsistent briefs and informal notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling and approval features handle coordination. Bounded extraction and drafting can reduce document work, and AI-assisted coding can shorten the build of missing links.
tasks.still_hard: Stakeholders may conceal constraints or disagree about success. Sources can be incomplete, and formal agreement still takes time.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unspoken concerns, negotiate competing goals and distinguish polite assent from commitment.

ambition.what: Monthly scope trade-off review using unresolved requirements and delivery evidence.

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less time preparing and rewriting workshops and more time resolving scope conflicts. They can propose scope trade-offs more often; sponsor approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Define measurable benefits for proposed requirements.
reach.learn: Benefit measures, process baselines and how to test whether a requirement changes outcomes.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, version control and approval routing can use existing system configuration.
Source-linked extraction and drafting can reduce preparation while leaving agreement to people.

assumptions: Time shares are indicative priors for a mid-size European company, not measured savings.
The conversation-heavy prior fits this decomposition; preparation remains separately changeable.
Build ranges estimate one pilot with existing identity controls and accessible files or interfaces.
Routine invitations use a confirmed participant list and a discussion brief cleared for those recipients.
GDPR applies to personal data. National rules determine consultation requirements if recording or monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Who can approve the requirements baseline?
Which sources contain client-confidential or employee personal data?
Are meeting notes available without introducing recording?
Which existing scheduling and approval features are enabled?
Which national rules and employee consultation arrangements apply?
research_questions: How reliably can extraction preserve disagreements and distinguish proposals from approved requirements?
Which requirement templates work across different project types without extensive customisation?
new_work: Review extracted constraints and drafted acceptance criteria.
Resolve missing sources and ambiguous agreement.
Maintain recipient permissions, templates and source links.
Check that amended requirements follow the approval route.
tasks.statement: Communicate with key stakeholders to determine project requirements and objectives.

tasks.short: Discuss project problems with the team and coordinate their resolution.

steps.what: Collect problem reports and clarify the reported impact.

loop.input: Selected problem reports and relevant project context.
loop.output: Issue summary with symptoms, reported impact, source links and missing facts.
loop.check: Preserve reported facts; mark conflicting accounts; do not infer a root cause or assign blame.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; missing facts go to the project manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reports use informal language and mix symptoms, opinions and incomplete facts.

steps.what: Check affected tasks, dependencies, owners and delivery dates.
Discuss causes and possible remedies with project personnel.
Choose a remedy within delegated authority or escalate the decision.
Record the agreed actions, owners, deadlines and closure criteria.

loop.input: Approved resolution decision and discussion notes.
loop.output: Proposed actions with owners, deadlines and closure criteria.
loop.check: Link every action to the decision; validate owner identifiers; require review of missing dates.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; incomplete actions stay drafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Agreed actions are often embedded in discussion notes rather than entered as structured records.

steps.what: Chase owners by message for updates already expected in task records.
Check resolution evidence and confirm whether the issue can close.

tasks.design: A bounded loop prepares source-linked issue summaries, and the {PROJECT} shows affected dependencies before the team discusses remedies. After human approval, a second bounded extraction writes agreed actions into the {PROJECT}; configured exception notifications replace routine chasing, while technical closure stays with the technical lead.
tasks.previous_blocker: Symptoms and agreements were scattered across messages and meetings. Issue records were often updated after the discussion, creating duplicate status requests.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing task views and notifications cover dependency checks and follow-up. Bounded extraction can turn selected reports and agreed notes into reviewed records.
tasks.still_hard: Root causes can be disputed or technically uncertain. People may avoid reporting bad news, and owners still need to keep task records current.
tasks.human_edge: Create a candid discussion, separate technical disagreement from interpersonal conflict and secure credible commitments.

ambition.what: Cross-project recurring-problem clinic for shared operational blockers.

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less time reconstructing issues and requesting duplicate updates, leaving more time for resolution discussions and recurring problems. They can convene the clinic and recommend preventive changes; technical and budget authority do not expand automatically.

reach.task: Turn recurring project blockers into recovery options.
reach.learn: Failure scenarios, recovery dependencies and when a local workaround creates wider operational risk.

evidence.claim: Dependency views and exception notifications can use existing work-management configuration.
Bounded extraction can support issue preparation and action records without automating diagnosis or negotiation.

assumptions: Time shares and build ranges are indicative pilot estimates.
The conversation-heavy prior fits; records and routine follow-up still offer separate gains.
Routine chasing disappears only when task records provide timely updates; missing updates become exceptions.
Only selected project reports are processed, rather than unrestricted mailbox or chat monitoring.
Technical leads approve remedies within delegated authority; scope, spending and staffing changes follow their separate approval routes.
GDPR applies to project communications. National rules may require consultation for changed employee-data processing; worker evaluation would need separate EU AI Act assessment.
unknowns: Where are problem reports and resolution evidence currently stored?
Do task owners update status reliably?
Which remedies can technical leads authorise?
Which message sources may be processed and retained?
Who decides closure for nontechnical issues?
Which national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: How reliably can extraction distinguish symptoms, hypotheses and agreed actions?
Which notification rules reduce duplicate chasing without hiding stalled issues?
How can recurring problems be grouped without attributing unsupported blame?
new_work: Review extracted facts and proposed action records.
Handle missing updates and failed notification delivery.
Maintain issue categories, escalation rules and access permissions.
Check recurring-problem groupings against source evidence.
tasks.statement: Confer with project personnel to identify and resolve problems.

tasks.short: Prepare and present project status, risks, costs and decisions needed.

steps.what: Collect milestone progress, delivery dates and open issues from the {PROJECT}.
Reconcile the {ERP} cost export against the project budget in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Read team updates in the {EMAIL} and {CHAT} for risks and explanations.

loop.input: Project-scoped team updates and progress snapshot.
loop.output: Status notes with source references, dates and unresolved contradictions.
loop.check: Require a source for each claim; check dates and identifiers; flag conflicting accounts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per reporting batch; unresolved items go to the project manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text updates describe causes and risks that fixed fields do not capture.

steps.what: Choose key messages and decisions for the presentation in the {DOCS}.
Build slides, charts and supporting detail in the {DOCS}.
Check accuracy, confidential detail and readiness to share the status presentation.
Present status and discuss decisions with the customer or project team.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration combines the {PROJECT} progress snapshot and {ERP} costs on the {DATA_PLATFORM}; a bounded loop extracts source-linked explanations from approved {EMAIL} and {CHAT} updates. A deterministic generator fills a presentation template in the {DOCS}, and the project manager approves disclosure and leads the discussion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress, costs and explanations sit in different places. Templates help layout but do not resolve conflicting updates.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, stable project identifiers and cheaper integration development make assembly feasible. Bounded extraction can reduce reading while preserving source references.
tasks.still_hard: Late updates, disputed progress and politically sensitive messages still need investigation. Customer-facing claims require careful review.
tasks.human_edge: Choose which problem deserves attention and explain difficult trade-offs without losing trust.

ambition.what: A twice-weekly delivery recovery decision for threatened milestones.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from slide assembly toward investigating delivery risks and preparing recovery options. Approval and customer commitment rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Compare recovery options for a delayed milestone.
reach.learn: Scenario analysis, assumption testing and concise decision briefs.

evidence.claim: Project reporting can combine deterministic data assembly with bounded extraction of narrative updates.
A documented report failure involving invented sources supports source checks on generated narrative.

assumptions: The baseline is a mid-size European company with project tracking, finance exports and document templates.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
Build ranges cover one reporting template and a limited set of source systems; they are working-day estimates.
Consultation time applies if staff-data use changes under national rules; elapsed approval time may be longer.
unknowns: Whether project and finance records share stable identifiers.
Which updates are approved for processing and which audiences may see them.
Whether existing reporting configuration already covers the presentation.
Which national rules and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can existing {PROJECT} reporting populate the required presentation template?
How reliably does extraction preserve disagreement and source dates in representative updates?
new_work: Review extracted explanations and unresolved contradictions.
Maintain project mappings, template sections and audience permissions.
Check generated charts after source or budget changes.
tasks.statement: Create project status presentations for delivery to customers or project personnel.

tasks.short: Develop and maintain an approved project plan covering scope, schedule, funding, technology and staffing.

steps.what: Read the brief, commitments and constraints before planning.

loop.input: Approved project brief, client commitments and technical constraints.
loop.output: Structured objectives, requirements, constraints and unresolved questions with source references.
loop.check: Validate required fields and source references; the project manager confirms interpretations and conflicts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document batch; unresolved conflicts return to the project manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative briefs express commitments and constraints inconsistently; fixed field mappings miss their meaning.

steps.what: Agree scope, delivery approach, technical choices and acceptance criteria.
Build activities, dependencies, milestones and a feasible delivery schedule.
Calculate staffing, procurement costs, funding needs and contingency.
Assemble the plan, assumptions, risks and responsibilities.
Review trade-offs and approve the project baseline.
Publish the approved baseline and notify delivery owners.

tasks.design: A bounded extraction loop turns approved material in the {DOCS} into source-linked planning inputs. Configure dependency scheduling in the {PROJECT}; deterministic calculations combine accepted estimates with rates from the {ERP} and capacity from the {HCM}, then generate a versioned plan in the {DOCS}. Approval in the {WORKFLOW} permits baseline publication and owner notifications.
tasks.previous_blocker: Narrative requirements, resource assumptions and cost calculations lived separately. Plan changes required repeated copying and reconciliation across documents and schedules.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can prepare inconsistent briefs for review. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of calculation, validation and document-generation glue; scheduling still uses established algorithms.
tasks.still_hard: People must supply credible estimates and resolve technical, staffing and funding trade-offs. Deterministic schedules can appear precise despite uncertain assumptions.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a workable delivery approach, challenge optimistic estimates and secure real resource commitments.

ambition.what: Weekly selection between recovery schedules within the approved scope and funding envelope.

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends more time testing alternatives with delivery leads and less time rebuilding plans. They gain faster choices within existing tolerances; scope, funding and baseline approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Identify material and production constraints affecting project milestones.
reach.learn: Learn lead-time variability, capacity calendars and dependency escalation.

reach.task: Plan technical dependencies, testing windows and release readiness.
reach.learn: Learn technical estimation uncertainty and release acceptance requirements.

evidence.claim: Dependency scheduling, cost calculations and template generation are established deterministic techniques.
A bounded extraction loop can prepare narrative planning inputs, subject to source and interpretation checks.
The digest provides no direct project-planning deployment case; time and build estimates remain unvalidated.

assumptions: Delivery leads provide effort estimates and technical choices; the model does not invent them.
One project type and one approval route are included in the initial build.
Only necessary capacity data is exposed; employee consultation under national rules may extend the access range.
Plan updates use the same preparation flow; baseline changes follow approval tolerances.
unknowns: Which scheduling and resource features are already configured?
Are rates, working calendars and capacity records reliable and accessible?
Who approves baselines and changes at each tolerance?
Which document formats, languages and technical constraints must be supported?
research_questions: Can existing scheduling configuration meet the required capacity constraints?
Which requirements need interpretation rather than direct field mapping?
How well do generated schedules reproduce accepted historical plans using the same inputs?
Which cost and capacity connectors justify their maintenance cost?
new_work: Review extracted commitments and resolve conflicting requirements.
Maintain rate mappings, planning templates and working calendars.
Investigate infeasible schedules and missing resource commitments.
Check baseline versions and approval references.
Reassess estimates when assumptions change.
tasks.statement: Develop or update project plans including information such as objectives, technologies, schedules, funding, and staffing.

tasks.short: Estimate project staffing, resource and funding needs from objectives and schedules.

steps.what: Review objectives and schedules to identify required work and capabilities.

loop.input: Requirements baseline and project schedule.
loop.output: Source-linked work requirements, capability needs and missing assumptions.
loop.check: Match each requirement to approved scope; require review for inferred effort or capabilities.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; uncertain requirements remain flagged for the planning discussion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Project objectives often describe outcomes in prose rather than explicit resource categories.

steps.what: Check team availability, existing assignments and approved resource capacity.
Check approved funding, committed costs and applicable cost rates.
Calculate effort, resource gaps and costs for alternative delivery plans.
Discuss feasibility and choose assumptions for the proposed resource plan.
Record and submit the staffing, resource and funding request.

tasks.design: A deterministic job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins authorised capacity from the {PROJECT} and {HCM} with funding and rates from the {ERP}, then calculates resource scenarios. A bounded loop extracts needs from approved documents in the {DOCS}; the project manager reviews assumptions and releases a resource request through the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Capacity and funding used different identifiers and update cycles. Effort assumptions were held in local workbooks or people's heads.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and interfaces can support repeatable joins and calculations. Bounded document extraction and faster custom coding make a small planning service more feasible.
tasks.still_hard: Availability may omit informal commitments. Effort estimates, specialist scarcity and competing projects still require negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a team can deliver together and recognise when apparently available capacity is unusable.

ambition.what: Weekly resource-gap review comparing scope reduction, sequencing and additional capacity.

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less time assembling numbers and more time testing delivery options with technical leads. They gain faster recommendation cycles; staffing allocation and spending authority require separate approval.

reach.task: Check competing work against shared capacity constraints.
reach.learn: Capacity calendars, bottleneck analysis and the difference between available hours and usable capacity.

evidence.claim: Capacity joins, rate calculations and scenario comparisons are suitable for deterministic code.
Extracting capability needs from project prose can use a bounded loop with human review.
AI used for worker evaluation or certain task-allocation purposes may fall within Annex III employment provisions.

assumptions: Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not documented project-management results.
The gathering and calculation steps show greater deterministic potential than the judgement-heavy prior alone suggests.
Calculations use explicit effort assumptions and approved rates; the model does not invent estimates.
Capacity data excludes absence reasons and other unnecessary personal details.
The design does not rank workers or infer performance. Any such extension requires separate GDPR and EU AI Act assessment.
Access estimates include employee consultation where national rules require it; formal processes may exceed the range.
Resource requests do not themselves authorise hiring, spending or employee reassignment.
unknowns: Are resource calendars complete and current?
Can project identifiers be matched across the {PROJECT} and {ERP}?
Which cost rates and effort assumptions are approved?
Who approves resource allocation and additional funding?
Which employee data may the project manager access?
Which national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which deterministic capacity rules remain useful across project types?
How should uncertainty ranges be calibrated against completed projects?
Which proposed staffing features would trigger employment-related EU AI Act obligations?
new_work: Correct unmatched project and resource identifiers.
Maintain cost rates, capacity rules and effort assumptions.
Review missing commitments and implausible scenarios.
Monitor data freshness and reconcile scenario estimates with completed work.
tasks.statement: Identify project needs such as resources, staff, or finances by reviewing project objectives and schedules.

tasks.short: Define supplier needs, compare vendors or consultants, assess fit, and secure an approved selection.

steps.what: Agree project requirements, selection criteria, and spending limits.
Review supplier records and capability documents to form a shortlist.

loop.input: Approved supplier records and capability documents matched to explicit requirements.
loop.output: Candidate shortlist with cited capability evidence and missing information.
loop.check: Apply eligibility rules deterministically; verify cited passages and review exclusions.
loop.stop: One extraction per document and one repair within document and token limits; uncertain cases go to procurement.
loop.why_not_simpler: Eligibility fields support filters, but capability evidence often appears only in free-text documents.

steps.what: Send standard requests for proposals to shortlisted suppliers.
Compare received proposals, prices, exclusions, and delivery commitments.

loop.input: Supplier proposals and the approved comparison schema.
loop.output: Evidence-linked comparison with prices, exclusions, commitments, and gaps.
loop.check: Recalculate totals deterministically; verify currencies, tax treatment, units, and source passages.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per proposal within a fixed token budget; unresolved fields remain blank.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposals use different layouts and prose for scope exclusions and delivery commitments.

steps.what: Test supplier fit through clarification calls, references, and commercial discussions.
Approve the preferred supplier and commercial limits.
Send the approved selection notice with its contractual conditions.
File the evaluation and open the contracting handoff.

tasks.design: The {PROCUREMENT} holds requirements, eligibility rules, supplier records, and approval limits; bounded extraction loops turn capability documents and proposals from the {DOCS} into cited comparisons. People assess fit and negotiate, while configured workflows gate external requests and notices and pass the approved selection to the {CLM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier evidence arrives in inconsistent documents and mail threads. Evaluation criteria and approval records are often scattered.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded document extraction can populate a fixed comparison schema. AI-assisted coding makes validation and document connectors cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: References can be selective, delivery capability is uncertain, and attractive proposals can conceal commercial dependencies.
tasks.human_edge: Testing credibility, understanding team fit, negotiating commitments, and defending a fair selection.

ambition.what: Evidence-based consideration of smaller suppliers outside the incumbent shortlist

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends more time testing supplier capability and less time copying proposal details. Selection and spending rights remain with their current holders.

reach.task: Assess supplier concentration and continuity exposure.
reach.learn: Supplier dependency mapping, financial resilience signals, and contingency options.

evidence.claim: Pactum's SUEZ case documents procurement requisition review automation; it does not establish autonomous project supplier selection.
Fixed comparison schemas, arithmetic checks, and approval routing can be deterministic; qualitative supplier fit still requires judgement.

assumptions: A procurement specialist supports project sourcing, with proposals commonly arriving through the {EMAIL}.
The solution compares suppliers and does not evaluate individuals for employment.
Selection notices use approved wording and do not bypass contracting authority.
GDPR applies to personal contact and reference data; employment-related consultant evaluation requires separate EU AI Act assessment.
Time shares and remaining effort are estimates; build ranges cover a pilot rather than every supplier category.
Access and consultation ranges represent working effort; national requirements and elapsed waits vary.
unknowns: Whether consultant selection includes recruitment or worker evaluation.
Which supplier sources may be searched and retained.
How conflicts of interest, eligibility, and spending limits are recorded.
Whether existing supplier records cover smaller or new suppliers adequately.
research_questions: Which native sourcing features support evidence-linked comparisons and approval routing?
How reliably can extraction distinguish fixed fees, estimates, exclusions, and optional work?
new_work: Verify extracted exclusions and commercial qualifications.
Review shortlist omissions and incomplete supplier evidence.
Maintain comparison schemas, eligibility rules, and notice templates.
Monitor access permissions and retention of supplier contact and reference data.
tasks.statement: Identify, review, or select vendors or consultants to meet project needs.

tasks.short: Track project staff costs and investigate budget variances.

steps.what: Collect recorded staff time, booked costs and expenses from the {PROJECT}, {ERP} and {EXPENSE}.
Map project codes and cost categories and resolve duplicates in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Compare costs with the project budget and calculate variances in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Discuss unexplained variances and missing entries with the finance team and workstream leads.
Record the budget issue, owner and proposed response in the {PROJECT}.
Notify the project sponsor and finance team of the budget issue through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: An integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles approved {PROJECT}, {ERP} and {EXPENSE} records and feeds a budget dashboard in the {BI}. Configured rules open exceptions in the {PROJECT} and notify approved internal recipients through the {EMAIL}; people investigate causes, while budget changes and accounting corrections follow their existing approval routes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Project codes, booking dates and cost definitions differ between sources. Manual reconciliation hides missing data and double-counted expenses.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduled exports and explicit mapping rules can replace repeated reconciliation. Existing dashboard and notification configuration covers much of the output.
tasks.still_hard: Unbooked time, delayed expenses and changing cost rates can distort the picture. A variance alone does not explain its cause or justify a staffing decision.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish timing differences from delivery problems and challenge assumptions with finance and technical leads.

ambition.what: A weekly corrective-action decision on unexplained staff-cost variance.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting and calculating costs toward investigating exceptions and preparing corrective options. Budget, staffing and accounting approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Explain cost drivers and test a revised project forecast.
reach.learn: Accruals, rate effects, forecast assumptions and sensitivity analysis.

reach.task: Compare shared-resource costs across projects.
reach.learn: Allocation methods and the limits of comparing unlike projects.

evidence.claim: Structured cost reconciliation, variance calculations and threshold alerts can use deterministic technology.
GDPR Article 22 concerns solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects; cost reporting alone does not establish such a decision.
Dutch works-council consent provisions cover specified staff-data and monitoring arrangements; other countries require their own national-rule assessment.

assumptions: The baseline uses system records with a spreadsheet reconciliation layer.
Finance-approved cost rates are used instead of exposing individual payroll details.
Reports focus on project costs and do not score employee performance or decide staffing actions.
GDPR applies to personal data; EU AI Act classification needs reassessment if worker evaluation is later introduced.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for an initial cost feed, mapping and dashboard.
Access and consultation work is included; elapsed consultation time can exceed the estimated effort.
unknowns: Whether the {ERP} already provides a complete project-cost and variance view.
Where staff time and approved cost rates are held.
How expenses, accruals and posted costs overlap.
Which recipients may see staff-level versus aggregated costs.
Which national consultation rules apply to the proposed data use.
research_questions: Can existing {ERP} configuration eliminate the reconciliation layer?
Which reconciliation checks detect missing periods, duplicate expenses and stale rates?
What project-level aggregation still supports useful investigation?
new_work: Resolve unmapped costs, missing periods and duplicate records.
Maintain cost mappings, approved rates and alert thresholds.
Review access permissions and source-feed failures.
Explain false alerts caused by booking delays or accrual changes.
tasks.statement: Monitor costs incurred by project staff to identify budget issues.

tasks.short: Track milestones and delivery evidence, assess readiness and record acceptance or exceptions.

steps.what: Check milestone dates, owners and acceptance criteria in the project records.
Locate submitted deliverables, test results and approval records.
Read evidence against acceptance criteria and identify gaps.

loop.input: Textual delivery evidence and approved acceptance criteria.
loop.output: Draft criterion-to-evidence map, apparent gaps and uncertain matches.
loop.check: Verify source passages and document versions; a person checks each claimed match and unresolved criterion.
loop.stop: One mapping and one repair attempt per deliverable; unsupported formats and ambiguous criteria go to specialist review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative evidence may describe criteria in different words. Exact test results and signed approvals use deterministic checks.

steps.what: Refresh the milestone variance sheet using dates, progress and evidence gaps.
Review readiness with the deliverable owner and obtain the acceptance decision.
Record the approved milestone status and notify owners of exceptions.

tasks.design: An integration links milestone records in {PROJECT} to versioned evidence in {DOCS}, while deterministic calculations replace the variance workbook with a {BI} view. A bounded loop maps narrative evidence to acceptance criteria and shows unresolved gaps. Approved acceptance decisions update {PROJECT} and trigger exception notifications through {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dates were structured, but evidence links and acceptance records were scattered. A separate workbook reconciled them, and automated status could not establish genuine readiness.
tasks.enabler_now: Document identifiers and accessible interfaces make evidence indexing practical. AI-assisted coding can simplify the integration work, with bounded reading reserved for narrative evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Evidence quality, vague acceptance criteria and specialist testing remain costly. A complete document set does not establish that the deliverable works.
tasks.human_edge: The project manager challenges optimistic status claims and brings the right specialist into acceptance decisions.

ambition.what: A self-service milestone readiness view for small internal project owners.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less evidence searching and workbook reconciliation, with more attention to disputed readiness and upcoming handovers. Acceptance rights remain with the accountable deliverable owner.

reach.task: Define evidence needed to accept a deliverable.
reach.learn: Test coverage, traceability and the difference between evidence presence and demonstrated quality.

reach.task: Maintain versioned delivery and approval records.
reach.learn: Document identifiers, retention rules and reliable evidence links.

evidence.claim: Milestone variance calculations and evidence indexing are deterministic when identifiers and baseline dates are reliable.
Narrative evidence mapping can assist review but cannot replace specialist tests or accountable acceptance.
The proposed implementation and remaining-time estimates have no direct documented case in the supplied digest.

assumptions: This typical hybrid process uses a {SPREADSHEET} to reconcile milestone dates and document evidence.
The workbook is integration glue; the authoritative schedule remains in {PROJECT}.
Deliverables have stable identifiers and approved acceptance criteria.
The bounded loop handles textual evidence; specialist technical validation stays separate.
The dashboard labels unreviewed assessments as provisional.
Build ranges cover a pilot with a limited set of evidence formats and exclude external waiting.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Access to personal data and any national consultation requirements need local assessment.
unknowns: Whether milestone tracking actually uses a workbook or native {PROJECT} reporting.
How consistently documents identify their project, milestone and version.
Which roles approve acceptance and whether approvals are recorded.
Which evidence formats require specialist systems or restricted access.
research_questions: Can deterministic metadata checks reliably identify missing or obsolete evidence?
Does narrative mapping falsely treat partial evidence as satisfying a criterion?
Can the readiness view help occasional project owners identify the next required action?
new_work: Review uncertain criterion-to-evidence matches.
Maintain evidence mappings and acceptance templates.
Repair broken links and obsolete document references.
Audit provisional statuses and recorded acceptance decisions.
tasks.statement: Monitor project milestones and deliverables.

tasks.short: Review project contributions, discuss performance and agree support or improvement actions.

steps.what: Review assigned work, deliverables and recorded project commitments.
Ask the team member about blockers, workload and missing context.
Assess contribution against agreed expectations and relevant context.
Prepare specific feedback examples and proposed support actions.
Give feedback, hear the response and agree practical support actions.
Record agreed actions, employee response and the next review date.

tasks.design: Configure a restricted view in the {PROJECT} that brings together agreed commitments and accepted deliverables. tasks.design: Configured availability rules in the {CALENDAR} replace availability chasing and book routine internal meetings. Bounded loops prepare agendas and minutes from the {PROJECT} and written notes in the {DOCS}; the project manager facilitates discussion and approves the record before agreed actions enter the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability chasing, meeting preparation, and action entry were separate routines. Informal notes did not provide reliable structured inputs.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing calendar configuration handles routine booking. Bounded drafting and structured action fields connect the surrounding paperwork at modest build cost.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting priorities, power differences, and unclear commitments require active human facilitation.
tasks.human_edge: Getting the right people to speak, noticing unresolved disagreement, and securing explicit commitments.

ambition.what: An asynchronous decision queue for contributors who cannot attend project meetings

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less time arranging meetings and more time resolving disagreement. Decision rights remain with the existing participants and sponsors.

reach.task: Coordinate decision agendas across senior stakeholders.
reach.learn: Agenda prioritisation, escalation etiquette, and calendar constraints.

evidence.claim: Availability rules, calendar invitations, approval routing, and action creation can use existing configuration.
The digest provides no direct meeting-facilitation automation case; the design preserves human facilitation.

assumptions: Routine meetings are internal and participants expose usable free/busy information through the {CALENDAR}.
Booking follows agreed working hours, required attendance, and rescheduling limits.
Written facilitator notes are used; recording and employee monitoring are outside the design.
Confirmed actions are stored as structured fields alongside approved minutes.
Time shares preserve substantial human meeting time despite the administrative automation opportunity.
Build ranges cover a pilot; national consultation requirements and access approval waits vary.
unknowns: Whether free/busy access covers all required participants.
Which meetings include external participants or confidential topics.
Who may publish minutes and confirm disputed commitments.
Whether national rules require consultation for the proposed note-processing arrangement.
research_questions: Which native booking features satisfy mandatory-attendee and working-hour constraints?
How should action updates avoid duplicates when approved minutes are corrected?
new_work: Review agenda priorities and ambiguous draft minutes.
Handle calendar conflicts that cannot satisfy booking rules.
Maintain participant permissions and document retention settings.
Resolve disputed commitments and correct linked project actions.
tasks.statement: Schedule or facilitate project meetings.

tasks.short: Check, present and submit project deliverables to clients.

steps.what: Collect the delivery version, acceptance criteria and quality evidence.
Check required files, version identifiers and recorded quality results.
Judge fitness for delivery and approve quality exceptions.
Assemble the client package and submission cover note.
Present the deliverable and explain limitations and acceptance arrangements.
Verify recipients and release the approved package to the client.
Record submission evidence and the next acceptance milestone.

tasks.design: The {PROJECT} and {DOCS} assemble a versioned delivery candidate, run explicit completeness checks and generate the submission package from a template. Technical sign-off enables release, the project manager approves the recipient and package in the {WORKFLOW}, and the {EMAIL} submission creates a receipt in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Delivery files, quality evidence and client requirements were stored separately. Manual assembly and mailbox records obscured which version had been approved and sent.
tasks.enabler_now: Version controls, templates and approval flows already cover much of the work. Small deterministic checks can connect these features without needing a model.
tasks.still_hard: Quality criteria vary by deliverable. A complete package can still be unsuitable, and disputed client acceptance requires human handling.
tasks.human_edge: Explain limitations honestly, judge whether exceptions are acceptable and preserve trust when a client is dissatisfied.

ambition.what: Client handover clinic for users who must operate the delivered service.

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less time finding files and reconstructing submission history, leaving time for practical client handover. They can propose the handover clinic; technical release and contractual acceptance rights remain with their existing owners.

reach.task: Define evidence required for a project delivery release.
reach.learn: Traceability, exception severity and the distinction between checklist completeness and fitness for use.

evidence.claim: Versioned files, template assembly and approval-dependent submission support deterministic automation.
Completeness checks can reduce paperwork but cannot establish fitness for use for every deliverable.

assumptions: Time shares and build ranges estimate a pilot for one deliverable family.
The prior's coordination-heavy pattern fits, but package assembly and submission records offer substantial deterministic savings.
Required quality tests already exist; the build checks their evidence rather than creating every domain test.
The cover note uses structured fields and approved wording, so no model loop is needed.
Client feedback does not establish formal acceptance unless the contract says it does.
GDPR governs personal data in delivery packages; access and retention follow contractual requirements and applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which deliverables and quality evidence are mandatory?
Who may approve quality exceptions and client release?
What constitutes contractual submission and acceptance?
Which recipients may access each delivery package?
Can the {DOCS} preserve the released version and access evidence?
Does the process change require employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Which formal delivery checks can be reused across service and technical projects?
Which submission channels provide sufficient evidence under common contract terms?
new_work: Maintain delivery checklists and submission templates.
Investigate missing evidence and failed version checks.
Review recipient access before release.
Handle failed transmissions, client objections and acceptance exceptions.
tasks.statement: Submit project deliverables to clients, ensuring adherence to quality standards.

role_batches.altitude: The week shifts from assembling briefs, reconciling planning data and chasing records toward scope trade-offs, resource discussions and client handover. The project manager gains faster access to options and evidence; formal spending, staffing, quality and acceptance rights remain separately assigned.
reach: Management analysts: connect requirements to measurable benefits.
Production planning clerks: compare shared capacity and bottlenecks.
Quality control systems managers: define release evidence and exception thresholds.
Business continuity planners: develop recovery options for recurring blockers.
skills_to_grow: Write testable requirements and explicit planning assumptions.
Interpret capacity and cost scenarios without treating estimates as facts.
Facilitate disagreement and negotiate credible commitments.
Design approval routes, exception rules and evidence checks.
Review source-linked model drafts and maintain proportionate data access.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide a lightweight project decision service: regular scope and resource reviews, practical client handover clinics and cross-project problem clinics. Start with reusable templates and authorised file imports, then add integrations where access and demonstrated value justify them.

role_batches.altitude: The project manager spends less time reconciling records and more time negotiating dependencies, resolving blockers and challenging readiness. Wider authority requires explicit sponsor or line-manager delegation; automation alone grants none.
reach: Production planning: connect project promises to real operational capacity.
Quality management: define acceptance evidence and organise specialist review.
Management analysis: compare recovery options and identify recurring delay causes.
Administrative services: coordinate shared capacity and reliable action records.
skills_to_grow: Dependency modelling and scenario comparison.
Clear acceptance criteria and evidence review.
Facilitation, escalation and recovery negotiation.
Data quality, integration ownership and exception handling.
Privacy-aware use of staffing data and national consultation requirements.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a small delivery-assurance service that gives occasional project owners schedule options, early blocker reviews and evidence-backed readiness views, with named people retaining commitment and acceptance decisions.

role_batches.altitude: Project managers spend less time assembling documents and reconciling costs, and more time testing recovery options, resolving resource conflicts and preparing decisions. Sponsors, document owners and procurement managers retain their existing approval rights.
reach: Management analyst: compare recovery scenarios and explain project cost drivers.
Administrative assistant: coordinate approvals and controlled document distribution.
Supply chain manager: assess resource alternatives and delivery risk.
File clerk: improve project records, classification and retrieval.
skills_to_grow: Project data definitions and reconciliation.
Scenario analysis and financial forecasting.
Source-based review of generated text.
Negotiation mandates and commercial trade-offs.
Document permissions, retention and release controls.
GDPR and applicable national employee consultation rules.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide a weekly project decision service that combines delivery risks, staff-cost variance and resource alternatives into concrete recovery options for sponsors.

role_batches.altitude: The project manager's week shifts toward delivery choices, staffing conversations and resolving exceptions. Preparation becomes faster, while hiring, employee assessment, funding and scope authority stay with their existing decision makers.
reach: Administrative services managers: coordinate readiness for confirmed project starters.
Management analysts: investigate recurring delivery barriers and portfolio patterns.
Information technology project managers: connect technical dependencies to delivery plans.
Business continuity planners: connect project disruptions to critical operations.
skills_to_grow: Define consistent project, cost and capacity data.
Test schedules and budgets against uncertain assumptions.
Review source-linked extraction and generated commentary.
Design approvals around consequential actions.
Give fair feedback using evidence and context.
Learn access, privacy and national employee consultation requirements.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide a recurring project decision service: compare recovery options, surface staffing gaps and bring sponsors specific choices before tolerances are breached. Earn any wider decision rights through explicit delegation and demonstrated delivery judgement.

role_batches.altitude: The project manager's week shifts from gathering records and producing paperwork toward testing delivery assumptions, resolving dependencies, and negotiating commitments. Existing sponsor, budget-owner, and procurement decision rights remain in place unless explicitly delegated.
reach: Management analyst: compare project outcomes and forecast reliability.
Supply chain manager: assess supplier dependency and continuity exposure.
Executive administrative assistant: coordinate decision agendas across senior stakeholders.
skills_to_grow: Scenario modelling and sensitivity analysis.
Cost reconciliation and forecast calibration.
Supplier evidence assessment and commercial judgement.
Facilitation, negotiation, and explicit commitment setting.
Data permissions, exception management, and automation acceptance checks.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide a cross-project decision service that combines current cost, dependency, and supplier evidence into comparable options for sponsors. The service recommends where intervention matters; accountable people approve commitments and changes.

summary.basis: 100 baseline hours; equal weight per loaded task; step shares normalized within each task
